summary:
[  edit  ]
The Speed  CHOP  converts speed (units per second) to distance (units) over a time range. More generally, you give it a rate (the  CHOP  input) and it outputs a cumulative value. For example, the Speed  CHOP  converts rotation rate (rotations per second) into the number of rotation turns. ( Math-heads recognize this as an 'integral', which calculates the area under a curve. The curve is the incoming channel values over a time range, the output is the area.)
If you send a Constant  CHOP  channel that has value 1 into the Speed  CHOP , then the Speed  CHOP  output will increase by 1 every second. If you feed it -2, it will decrease by 2 every second, and if you feed it 0, the output will not change. Use a Trail  CHOP  to see its results. You can reset the Speed  CHOP  to 0 by pressing the Reset parameter, or by sending in a channel (whose value is greater than 0) into the second input.
The first input contains the channels to be 'integrated'. By default, the Speed  CHOP  is time-sliced, so it keeps adding/subtracting to the output each frame it cooks. If you turn off its  Time Slice  parameter and send it a  CHOP  with a fixed frame range (like a default Noise  CHOP ), you can see the cumulative value starting from 0.
The output is calculated by adding the input's channel values for every sample, divided by the  samples per second  of the Speed  CHOP  (typically 60), starting with the sample at the Start index. Negative input values reduce the output, positive values increase it. The cumulative values are put in the output channels.
When the  CHOP  is reset, its output can be set to any value via the  Reset Value  parameter.
When the second input is used to reset the output, where the second input is greater than 0, the area is reset and held to the reset value. For example, a  Wave CHOP  (which is negative half the time) when passed into the second input causes the output to be reset for half a cycle.
See also:  Lookup CHOP ,  Timer CHOP ,  Count CHOP ,  Event CHOP

parameters.label: Order
parameters.name: order
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines the order of the integral to use. If the input is a velocity, a First Order integral will return the position. If the input is an acceleration, a Second Order integral will return the position, and a First Order integral will return the velocity.

parameters.label: Speed
parameters.name: speed
parameters.description: Allows generating values when no inputs are connected. This parameter is disabled as soon as an input is connected to the Speed  CHOP .

parameters.label: First Constant
parameters.name: constant1
parameters.description: Constant to add to the entire result after integrating once.

parameters.label: Second Constant
parameters.name: constant2
parameters.description: Constant to add to the entire result after integrating twice.

parameters.label: Third Constant
parameters.name: constant3
parameters.description: Constant to add to the entire result after integrating three times.

parameters.label: Limit Type
parameters.name: limittype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select limit options such as loop, clamp, or zigzag from the menu. The value will remain in the range from Min to less than Max.

parameters.label: Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Do not limit the values.

parameters.label: Clamp
parameters.name: clamp
parameters.description: Simply cut the channel value off if it is out of the Maximum/Minimum range, and replace it with the Maximum or Minimum limit value.

parameters.label: Loop
parameters.name: loop
parameters.description: Continue the channel at the other end of the interval.

parameters.label: Zigzag
parameters.name: zigzag
parameters.description: Mirror the values back inside the interval.

parameters.label: Minimum
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: The minimum value the output channel can have.

parameters.label: Maximum
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: The maximum value the output channel can have.

parameters.label: Speed per  Sample
parameters.name: speedsamples
parameters.description: Applies the speed to each sample of the channel instead of across the whole channel. Useful for working with multi-sample channels.

parameters.label: Reset Condition
parameters.name: resetcondition
parameters.description: ⊞  - This menu determines how the Reset input triggers a reset of the channel(s).

parameters.label: Off to On
parameters.name: offtoon
parameters.description: Channels are reset when the Reset input goes off to on.

parameters.label: While On
parameters.name: on
parameters.description: Channels are reset when the Reset input goes on. The channel will hold the reset value until the input turns off.

parameters.label: On to Off
parameters.name: ontooff
parameters.description: Channels are reset when the Reset input goes on to off.

parameters.label: While Off
parameters.name: off
parameters.description: Channels are reset when the Reset input goes off. The channel will hold the reset value until the input turns on.

parameters.label: Reset Value
parameters.name: resetvalue
parameters.description: The channel(s) is set to this value when reset.

parameters.label: Reset
parameters.name: reset
parameters.description: ⊞  - While On, this toggle resets the channel(s) to the  Reset Value .

parameters.label: Reset on Start
parameters.name: resetonstart
parameters.description: While On, the Speed  CHOP  will reset each time the  .toe  file is restarted. If the Speed  CHOP 's value gets too large it can start stepping as when it reaches the limit of  CHOP 's number resolution. This is useful for projects that run for a long time, restarting the file will reset this value.

parameters.label: Reset  Pulse

parameters.description: Click to instantly resets the channel(s) to the  Reset Value .

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

POPs vs. SOPs - **Execution**: POPs run on the GPU (parallelized compute shaders); SOPs run on the CPU. - **Workflow**: POPs combine strengths of SOPs, CHOPs, and TOPs for a modern approach. - **Attributes**: POPs offer advanced attribute manipulation (e.g., multi-component, high precision). - **Limitations**: POPs lack some SOP features (e.g., tracing, booleans), though these may be added later. ## 4. Key Features - **GPU Acceleration**: Uses compute shaders for speed and efficiency. - **Memory Optimization**: References unchanged attributes, allocating memory only for modified data. - **Math Operations**: POPs like `Math`, `Transform`, and `Normalize` enable coding-free manipulations. - **Multi-Input Support**: POPs like `Merge` and `Switch` handle multiple inputs with flexible configurations. - **Swizzling**: Manipulate attribute components (e.g., `P.xy` for X and Y). ## 5.
